cover: Aid centre bombed, at least 33 dead
Police officer fires on villagers, one dead
Police: Jantar Mantar never fit for protests

stories.label: World · Life & safety
stories.head: Aid centre bombed
bullets: Aerial bombs hit an aid distribution centre in a school building on Monday.
More than 50 people may be trapped under the rubble, President Zelensky said.
Russia's defence ministry says it targeted Ukrainian military units.
stories.caption:
People had gathered for aid when the bombs fell, officials say, and rescuers searched the rubble for survivors. Russia says it hit military units.
Source: BBC

stories.label: World · Life & safety
stories.head: Drone hits travellers' car
bullets: A drone struck a private vehicle carrying goods on Sunday; a third man survived.
A local rights monitor blames the army's drones.
stories.caption:
Two men carrying goods home to Al-Malha were killed on the road, a witness says; one victim's brother, riding with them, survived. The army has not commented.
Source: Radio Tamazuj

stories.label: India · Life & safety
stories.head: Police officer fires on villagers
bullets: An ASI fired four rounds from his service pistol early Tuesday after villagers confronted him, police say.
He has been suspended and faces a murder case.
Five police teams are searching for him; a Rs 25,000 reward is offered.
stories.caption:
A 50-year-old man died in hospital. Police say the officer will be dismissed; we are following the case on Accountability Watch.
Source: Indian Express

stories.label: India · Assembly
stories.head: Protest site 'never fit'
bullets: Delhi Police told the Supreme Court that Jantar Mantar is a public road and should never have been a protest site.
Police named three other grounds for protests.
Petitioners say the 11 October de-notification violates free speech and assembly.
stories.caption:
For years Jantar Mantar was where Delhi went to be heard. Police now say nearness to government no longer matters in the age of social media.
Source: Scroll
